cases.sentence: – В ___ предлагаю вам свою руку, – сказал он чрез несколько времени, обращаясь к ней.
cases.explain: «третий раз» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “For the third time I offer you my arm,” he said to her after a little time, turning to her. Anna gazed at him and did not know what to say. Princess Betsy came to her rescue.

cases.sentence: Несмотря на все, что он видел, Алексей Александрович все-таки не позволил себе думать о ___ своей жены.
cases.explain: «настоящем положении» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: She took her seat in her husband’s carriage in silence, and in silence drove out of the crowd of carriages. In spite of all he had seen, Alexey Alexandrovitch still did not allow himself to consider his wife’s real condition. He merely saw the outward symptoms. He saw that she was behaving unbecomingly, and considered it his duty to tell her so. But it was very difficult for him not to say more, to tell her nothing but that. He opened his mouth to tell her she had behaved unbecomingly, but he could not help saying something utterly different.

cases.explain: «внешние признаки» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.

cases.sentence: – Как, однако, мы все склонны к этим ___, – сказал он. – Я замечаю…
cases.explain: «жестоким зрелищам» — after the preposition «к», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “What an inclination we all have, though, for these cruel spectacles,” he said. “I observe. …”

cases.sentence: – Я уже просил вас держать себя в свете так, что ___ не могли ничего сказать против вас.
cases.explain: «злые языки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “I have already begged you so to conduct yourself in society that even malicious tongues can find nothing to say against you. There was a time when I spoke of your inward attitude, but I am not speaking of that now. Now I speak only of your external attitude. You have behaved improperly, and I would wish it not to occur again.”

cases.sentence: Было время, когда я говорил о ___; я ведь не говорю про них.
cases.explain: «внутренних отношениях» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “I have already begged you so to conduct yourself in society that even malicious tongues can find nothing to say against you. There was a time when I spoke of your inward attitude, but I am not speaking of that now. Now I speak only of your external attitude. You have behaved improperly, and I would wish it not to occur again.”

cases.sentence: Алексей Александрович не пошевелился и не изменил ___ взгляда.
cases.explain: «прямого направления» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: And dropping back into the corner of the carriage, she broke into sobs, hiding her face in her hands. Alexey Alexandrovitch did not stir, and kept looking straight before him. But his whole face suddenly bore the solemn rigidity of the dead, and his expression did not change during the whole time of the drive home. On reaching the house he turned his head to her, still with the same expression.

cases.sentence: Но я требую соблюдения ___ приличия до тех пор, – голос его задрожал, – пока я приму меры, обеспечивающие мою честь, и сообщу их вам.
cases.explain: «внешних условий» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Very well! But I expect a strict observance of the external forms of propriety till such time”—his voice shook—“as I may take measures to secure my honor and communicate them to you.”

cases.sentence: Еще оставалось три часа, и воспоминания подробностей ___ зажгли ей кровь.
cases.explain: «последнего свидания» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: She glanced at her watch. She had still three hours to wait, and the memories of their last meeting set her blood in flame.

cases.sentence: Это страшно, но я люблю видеть его лицо и люблю этот ___…
cases.explain: «фантастический свет» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: “My God, how light it is! It’s dreadful, but I do love to see his face, and I do love this fantastic light. … My husband! Oh! yes. … Well, thank God! everything’s over with him.”
